svg.title: Track One Cohort from Alert to Cash
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-qualified-lot-conversion; chart type: funnel; title: Track One Cohort from Alert to Cash; subtitle: A nested 200-lot cohort with six completed resale collections; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative 120-day observation window, not a forecast of market conversion rates or a promise of first-month sales. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; count each lot once. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–6 months.; caption: The two awarded but uncollected lots remain inventory or unsettled dispositions; they do not become collected resale proceeds merely because an auction was won.; stages: label: Unique alerted lots; value: 200 lots enter review; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Deduplicate reposted listings and capture seller, asset class, location, closing date, and pickup window. This is the complete cohort denominator.; label: Desk-qualified lots; value: 80 lots; 40% of alerts; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Retain only lots within the operating radius, capital limit, permitted asset categories, and documented buyer demand. Exclude inaccessible removal sites and unresolved ownership restrictions.; label: Inspection-cleared lots; value: 24 lots; 30% of qualified; numeric value: 24.0; detail: Complete condition verification, document review, transport quotations, and repair estimates. These 24 lots receive evidence-backed bid ceilings; inspection expense also includes unsuccessful bids.; label: Awarded and paid lots; value: 8 lots; 33.3% of cleared; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Win eight lots without exceeding their ceilings and settle their purchase invoices. Reject price chasing; the other sixteen cleared lots consume inspection effort but no acquisition principal.; label: Resold and collected lots; value: 6 lots; 75% of awarded; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Collect resale proceeds on six of the eight acquired lots within the observation window. Overall alert-to-collection conversion is 3%; track the remaining two lots through inventory aging.

text.title: Track One Cohort from Alert to Cash
text.tspan: Track One Cohort from Alert to Cash

circle.title: label: Unique alerted lots; value: 200 lots enter review; numeric value: 200.0; detail: Deduplicate reposted listings and capture seller, asset class, location, closing date, and pickup window. This is the complete cohort denominator.

label: Desk-qualified lots; value: 80 lots; 40% of alerts; numeric value: 80.0; detail: Retain only lots within the operating radius, capital limit, permitted asset categories, and documented buyer demand. Exclude inaccessible removal sites and unresolved ownership restrictions.

label: Inspection-cleared lots; value: 24 lots; 30% of qualified; numeric value: 24.0; detail: Complete condition verification, document review, transport quotations, and repair estimates. These 24 lots receive evidence-backed bid ceilings; inspection expense also includes unsuccessful bids.

label: Awarded and paid lots; value: 8 lots; 33.3% of cleared; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Win eight lots without exceeding their ceilings and settle their purchase invoices. Reject price chasing; the other sixteen cleared lots consume inspection effort but no acquisition principal.

label: Resold and collected lots; value: 6 lots; 75% of awarded; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Collect resale proceeds on six of the eight acquired lots within the observation window. Overall alert-to-collection conversion is 3%; track the remaining two lots through inventory aging.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative 120-day observation window, not a forecast of market conversion rates or a promise of first-month sales. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; count each lot once. The canonical time to first deal remains 1–6 months.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Illustrative 120-day observation window, not a forecast of market conversion rates or a promise of first-month sales.
